candidates.term: The Virtuoso inside the Month Gate
candidates.defline: The Virtuoso holds your strongest seat, inside your Month Gate: your working years run on seeing how everything could be better.
candidates.reading: You spot the better version of a plan, a process or a piece of work almost at once, and the weaker version nags at you for days. Because an unfixed flaw weighs on you more than hard work does, you keep improving things long after others call them finished, and you are still thinking about them at night. Managers find you tiring and colleagues find you useful, and you are proud of being both.
candidates.teaser: Your prime runs on performance: you outdo, outshine, and occasionally overstep. The money follows your gift wherever the format is loose and the spotlight honest.

domain_readings.Career: Improvement is your actual profession, whatever the title says: you see the better version instantly and cannot unsee it. Careers where revision is the job, editing, design, strategy, reform, pay you for what others endure in you. Aim the critique at systems. Systems thank you. People vary.
domain_readings.Mind: Your mind files the world under drafts: everything improvable, nothing finished, including your own positions. It is exhausting and it is a gift. Give it one worthy revision at a time and it produces mastery. Give it everything at once and it produces insomnia.

candidates.life_chapter: Your rising chapter revises: the prime decades hand you flawed systems and the compulsion to fix them, and your reputation builds on the upgrades. Expect restlessness as the era’s tax and mastery as its payout. One deep specialty calms what ten shallow ones inflame.
candidates.relations: The improvable are this seat’s people, which is everyone, and therein the lesson: colleagues who welcome your notes become allies for life, and the rest need your silence more than your insight. Learn the difference by thirty-five. It is the whole social curriculum.
candidates.turn_catalyst: Run thin, the critique swallows itself: improvements seen, unsaid, composting into frustration. Publish one fix this month, however small.
candidates.turn_friction: Run heavy, the red pen never caps: everything marked up, nothing enjoyed. Read one thing this week purely for pleasure.
candidates.shadow_line: Overloaded, the editor edits the editor: self-revision without a final draft.
candidates.health_line: The unfinished list lives in your body: sleep waits on solved problems. Write tomorrow’s revisions down tonight, and let the mind clock out.

Career.headline: You are paid to make things better.
Career.recognition: You are best in jobs where improving things is the work itself, editing or design or reform of some kind. Because a weak plan is plain to you before anyone asks, you correct work that was never yours to correct. Your value at work grows with every process you improve, and you are known as the colleague who will not let poor work pass.
Career.lived: In class, in teams and in your first jobs you have been the one who points out what could be better. You have clashed with at least one boss over it, and you have also been the person they sent for when something needed fixing.

Mind.headline: Your mind never stops improving what it sees.
Mind.recognition: You think in revisions, turning over a plan or an idea or your own opinion until it is better, and nothing feels quite finished to you. Since a fault you have noticed stays with you until it is mended, your mind keeps working when the day is over. You sleep best in the weeks when one hard problem has all of your attention.
Mind.lived: Your mind has gone looking for faults since your late teens, in what you were taught and in what you believed yourself. You have changed your view on something important more than once over those years, and each time you argued yourself into the new view first.
